scenes.heading: Catalyst Optimizer
scenes.narration: Let's take a deep look at Catalyst Optimizer and how it works under the hood in Spark.

scenes.heading: What Catalyst does
items: Turns SQL/DataFrame code into an optimized physical plan
scenes.narration: Catalyst is Spark SQL's query optimizer, the engine that converts your declarative DataFrame and SQL code into an efficient execution plan. It applies both rule-based rewrites, like pushing filters down, and cost-based choices, like picking a join strategy. The plan it produces is what the Tungsten engine ultimately runs.

scenes.heading: The four phases
scenes.narration: Catalyst moves your query through four phases. First it parses code into an unresolved logical plan, then analysis resolves column names and data types against the catalog. Next, logical optimization applies rules such as predicate pushdown, constant folding, and projection pruning. Finally, physical planning generates several candidate plans and uses cost estimates to select the one that executes.

scenes.code:
df = spark.read.parquet("/data/orders")
result = (df.select("id", "amount", "status")
            .filter(df.status == "PAID")
            .filter(df.amount > 100))
result.explain("formatted")
# Catalyst fuses both filters and pushes them to the scan
scenes.heading: Seeing optimization at work
scenes.narration: Notice we wrote two separate filters and a select in a natural order. Catalyst does not execute them literally; it combines both predicates and pushes them down to the Parquet scan so unmatched rows are never read. It also prunes columns so only id, amount, and status are loaded. The formatted explain output reveals these rewrites in the physical plan.

scenes.heading: Rule-based vs cost-based
scenes.narration: Catalyst blends two optimization styles. Rule-based optimization always fires deterministic rewrites like pushing predicates and pruning unused columns. Cost-based optimization, when statistics are available, chooses smarter join orders and strategies based on estimated data sizes. Running ANALYZE TABLE to collect statistics is what unlocks the cost-based decisions.

scenes.text: Write clear DataFrame code and let Catalyst optimize the how.
scenes.narration: Because Catalyst re-plans your entire query, favor declarative expressions over manual micro-optimizations. Keep table statistics fresh so the cost-based optimizer can help you.
